title: Use of Generative Artificial Intelligence by Production Engineering Students at the Federal University of Amazonas in the First Semester of 2026
content: This study analyzed Production Engineering students’ use of Generative Artificial Intelligence (GenAI) at FT/UFAM, Brazil, in the first semester of 2026 to support pedagogical decisions. This exploratory, descriptive, and quantitative study surveyed 106 of the 263 enrolled students through non-probability convenience sampling. Course- level responses were screened with consistency rules based on institutional documents and analyzed using descriptive statistics, a chi-square test, and generalized estimating equations. In all, 87.7% of respondents use GenAI, mainly ChatGPT and Gemini, to improve their writing and solve problems. Differences between semester blocks varied across data-screening scenarios, which precludes conclusions about a pattern of use throughout the program. Among users, 63% learned to use these tools on their own and only 16% from university instructors; 68% reported difficulties with GenAI literacy and 61% a lack of clear guidelines. Among respondents, widespread GenAI adoption contrasts with the limited role of instructors as a reported source of learning and with the absence of program- specific guidelines: the central challenge is not to introduce GenAI but to provide pedagogical guidance for a practice that is already widespread. We recommend combining AI literacy, explicit rules in course syllabi, and assessments that value the learning process and transparency of use.
